content: Hydroxyzine is a medication used for the short-term treatment of nervousness and tension associated with certain mental or mood disorders, such as anxiety and dementia. It is also utilized to manage withdrawal symptoms, including anxiety and agitation, in individuals with alcohol dependence. This drug belongs to a class of medications known as antihistamines. Its mechanism of action is thought to involve modulation of specific natural substances in the body, such as acetylcholine and serotonin, or direct effects on certain areas of the brain. This medication is administered via injection into a muscle as directed by a healthcare provider. If you are instructed to administer this medication at home, ensure you are thoroughly trained in its preparation and usage by a healthcare professional. Before use, visually inspect the product for any particles or discoloration. If either is present, do not use the liquid. Common side effects of hydroxyzine may include drowsiness, dizziness, blurred vision, dry mouth, constipation, or headache. It is important to note that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the potential risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, this is not an exhaustive list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar guidance. Before using hydroxyzine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, cetirizine, or levocetirizine, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other complications. Hydroxyzine may also lead to a condition affecting heart rhythm known as QT prolongation. The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other medications that can cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood can also elevate this risk, particularly if you are using certain drugs like diuretics or experiencing conditions such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. This medication may cause dizziness, drowsiness, or blurred vision. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness or clear vision until you can do so safely. Limit the consumption of alcoholic beverages. Older adults may be more sensitive to the side effects of this drug, particularly drowsiness, confusion, constipation, difficulty urinating, or QT prolongation. Children may also be more susceptible to the side effects of this medication. During pregnancy, hydroxyzine should only be used when clearly necessary. It is not known whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Check the labels on all your medications, such as allergy or cough-and-cold products, as they may contain ingredients that cause drowsiness. Hydroxyzine may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as allergy skin tests or urine corticosteroid tests, potentially leading to false results. If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. It is crucial to take each dose of this medication as scheduled. If you miss a dose, consult your doctor or pharmacist promptly for a new dosing schedule. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
